items.title: Eurreal Wilford "Little Brother" Montgomery Interview, 1958-05-29
items.q: So he got a band together. I was in the band, Zooty, and Earl, Joe Walker

ctx.x: So he leased the hall on 47, the old Warwick Hall. Oh yeah, I remember. And he got another hall on the west side. I don't remember, it was on Madison Street somewhere, I don't remember just the name of it. So he got a band together. I was in the band, Zooty, and Earl, Joe Walker, Lil' Joe Walker, Frank Sacks, and another boy, George Terence, was on Sacks. Was Lil in the band? No, Lil wasn't in the band, no. He was still married to Lil, but Lil wasn't in his band. Earl was there. Oh, that's right. That's right,…
I remember Zutty told me years ago, he said in place of being the hot six, they thought they'd better call it the hungry six.

items.title: Al Wynn Interview, 1958-05-29
items.q: go with Carol Dixon as a replacement at the Grand Terrace when Earl would go out on the road.

ctx.x: Well, we got the end of that story. And that's just something else that you think ought to be told, especially?

Well, there's nothing other than that when I come to Chicago. Nothing very much was happening here. I went with Jesse Stone. We finally got a band together and opened a new spot here, the Club Morocco. But they had a lot of hometown boys that didn't want to go any place. It was discontented. Never the type of Jimmy Noon now. Yeah, Jimmy Noon eventually went in the same place. So, uh, in the meantime, I leave Jimmy Stone and go with Carol Dixon as a replacement at the Grand Terrace when Earl would go out on the…
